text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Daniel arap Moi's son, Raymond Moi, cabinet ministers Simeon Nyachae and Kipkalya Kones and politician Nicholas Biwott, in collaboration with Kenya Commercial Bank, plan to buy the Kenya Cooperative Creameries at a throwaway price after ensuring its collapse, parliament is told.
- Two Rwandans, a former senior army officer and a businessman, were murdered by gunmen and their bodies dumped in Tigoni on the edge of Nairobi, police said.
- A bill seeking the creation of retirement benefits regulatory authority will be published soon, Labour Minister Philip Masinde says.
- Thirteen prisoners made a dramatic lunchtime escape from Nairobi law courts, grabbing guns from two policemen guarding them and leaving the magistrate stunned.
- Ruling KANU party votes to reject a freelance motion seeking to establish a select committee to probe giant milk company Kenya Cooperative Creameries.
- Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem gives President Moi 7.3 billion shillings being dividend payable to the exchequer in the financial year 1995/96.
